audit.why: HARD at 8/10 with an 8.5/10 carry threat matches a 34.38% win rate. Left alone, and it agrees with the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart hands Graves level 1 and level 6 and calls level 2 even. The packet chart is Skill / Malphite / Malphite / Malphite / Malphite / Malphite / Malphite, and every why agrees with it — including whys[4], which describes being knocked airborne at 6.
audit.why: A row saying Graves wins level 6 sits directly above a sentence explaining that Unstoppable Force combos you off the ground before you can dash. The mirror already rewrote its level-1 why around the reload window and Granite Shield, so the two sides must both read Skill at level 1.
audit.corrected: Both charts flipped as one atomic group, with Unstoppable Force's 130s, Seismic Shard's 8s and Ground Slam's 7s written into the phases.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ground Slam is never mentioned once on the entire page, and it is the ability that actually beats Graves in this lane.
audit.why: It reduces attack speed on a 7-second cooldown. Graves' whole pattern is landing basic attacks, and Riot's Quickdraw text says hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers its cooldown and refreshes the resistance boost. So Ground Slam does not just cut his damage — it slows the reload cycle AND delays the dash he needs to leave with. One ability taxes his DPS, his escape and his resistances at the same time.
audit.corrected: Written into phases[3], the mid block and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Smoke Screen is called a blind four times, including the line 'your W blind does nothing to his ability damage'. Graves' Q is called a 'Q cone' three times and a 'Q powder' twice. Collateral Damage is credited with a 'disengage knockback'.
audit.why: W reduces sight range and slows on impact — the mirror already restated this as nearsight, so both sides must agree. The cone belongs to Graves' R, not his Q; End of the Line is a single explosive shell with a 1-second fuse. And nothing in Graves' kit knocks back a champion — his passive knocks back non-champions only.
audit.corrected: All three corrected in the strings I own, phrased to match the mirror's wording.

audit.whatIsWrong: Granite Shield's actual terms are never given, and neither is the minion-block rule the mirror added on its side.
audit.why: The shield absorbs up to 10% of his maximum health and recharges only if he has not been hit for a few seconds — so a single pellet between trades keeps it off, which is free value in a lane where nothing else is. And Graves' bullets cannot pass through units, so at level 1 the minion line between you is why his poke is one-way.
audit.corrected: Both written into whys[0], spikes[0] and phases[2], matching the mirror's addition from the other side.

edits.before: Malphite stacks armor and your entire kit is physical — your 4-shell spread, your Q cone, your R nuke all scale into the wrong stat. At Level 1 his Q powder pokes you with his Granite Shield up and your short shell range can't punish back through the gap. Your one window is Level 2-3: E in for the point-blank shell burst and drop W on him to blind a key auto, but his Q slow peels you out of magazine range the second you commit, and his passive shield soaks your opening poke. Don't burn both E charges chasing — you'll be stranded in his face with an empty magazine and no dash to leave on.
edits.after: Malphite stacks armor and your entire kit is physical — your 4-shell spread, End of the Line, your R nuke all scale into the wrong stat. At Level 1 Seismic Shard pokes you with Granite Shield up, and your bullets can't pass through the minion line, so you can't punish back. Your one window is Level 2-3: E in for the point-blank burst and drop W on him for the impact slow, but Seismic Shard steals your speed the second you commit and his shield eats 10% of his max HP off the top. edits.before: This only gets worse. Through Levels 4-5 your True Grit passive and E charges compound your tankiness, but you're stacking armor and MR to survive a lane you can't actually win on damage — every shell you land lands into his armor for less. At 6 his R Unstoppable Force is a dashing knockup he can't be peeled off: he engages, slows you with Q, and you're airborne and locked before you can E out, and your W blind does nothing against his ability damage. There is no all-in you win here — bait nothing, just farm safe and look for plays on other lanes.
edits.after: This only gets worse, and Ground Slam is why: every 7 seconds he cuts your attack speed, which is your damage AND the Quickdraw cooldown refund you get from landing autos — one ability taxes your DPS and your escape together. Through 4-5 your True Grit stacks keep you alive in a lane you can't win on damage anyway. At 6 Unstoppable Force is a 130-second dashing knockup he can't be peeled off: he engages, Seismic Shard steals your speed, and you're airborne before Quickdraw is back. Farm safe and look for plays elsewhere.

edits.before: Late game you are a pure-AD carry running into an armor tank who builds Frozen Heart and Thornmail specifically to delete you. Your shells, your Q cone and your R nuke are all physical and all answered by his armor stack — Thornmail even reflects every magazine you dump into him. Worse, his R is a permanent flank threat aimed at your squishy back line — facecheck a bush near an objective and his Unstoppable Force has you airborne and dead before your magazine reloads. Your only path is to have snowballed off-map earlier; if the game went long into him, this matchup is already lost.
edits.after: Late game you are a pure-AD carry running into an armor tank who builds Frozen Heart and Thornmail specifically to delete you. Your shells, End of the Line and your R nuke are all physical and all answered by his armor stack — and Frozen Heart's aura compounds the attack-speed cut Ground Slam already applies. Worse, his R is a permanent flank threat on your back line: facecheck a bush near an objective and Unstoppable Force has you airborne and dead before your magazine reloads. Your only path is to have snowballed off-map earlier.

notes: Mirror-consistent: the malphite__graves audit rewrote its level-1 why around the reload window and Granite Shield, added the bullets-blocked-by-units rule, and replaced 'blind' with nearsight. I have restated the same three facts from this side and set level 1 to Skill on both charts so the two pages agree. Following the mirror's finding, I did NOT write any grounding claim: Malphite's kit file derives 'grounding: shuts off enemy dashes' on both Seismic Shard and Ground Slam, and Riot's descriptions support only a move-speed steal and an attack-speed reduction. If Ground Slam really did ground, it would shut off Quickdraw entirely and change this matchup's advice — that is worth a human check, and it is in unverified.
